# Story view — build-atomic-card

*(DERIVED RENDERING — generated by `studio/tools/generate-story.py` from brief.md §4, workflow.fabro, and prompts/. Read it to see the whole play working together as one story; never run it, never edit it — re-derive it.)*

## The story

A **card contract** arrives — one
concept, one atomicity question, a target category, and the exact source ranges
that may ground it. The build first **validates the contract** mechanically; an
invalid contract emits a child result and stops. Then a GPT-5.4 agent **drafts
(or repairs) the card** — reading only the contract, the source ranges it cites,
and the existing card library, writing the five sections (WHAT · WHERE · WHY ·
WHEN · HOW) with wikilinks to genuinely-related cards and never a claim the source
doesn't support. A **candidate validator** checks the structure mechanically;
structural issues consume a revision turn and bounce back to the drafter. A second
GPT-5.4 agent **grades the candidate** against the rubric and the *raw* source,
returning a structured verdict — **PUBLISH**, **REVISE**, or **BAIL**. Publish
clears the contract's grade bar with no source-grounding violations; revise spends
a turn and sends specific deficiencies back to the drafter; bail means the source
simply can't support this card. When a verdict resolves or the turns are spent,
the build **publishes** (or doesn't) and **emits a child result** for the planning
play that called it.

## The golden path, move by move

### 1. `validate_contract` — Validate Contract

Routes besides the golden path: `Invalid` → `emit_child_result`

Software node — the script is the prompt:

```sh
cd '__AX_PROJECT_ROOT__' && ax2 cards validate-contract --contract '__AX_INPUT_CONTRACT_PATH__' --reset-attempts --json
```

### 2. `draft_or_repair` — Draft or Repair Card

```markdown
You are drafting one Alexandria atomic card from a card contract. Working directory: the Alexandria workspace. Read only the contract, the source ranges it references, the card library, and your candidate file; do not read any other file in the project. Contract file: '__AX_INPUT_CONTRACT_PATH__'. Read it first. Resolve every source reference with: cd '__AX_PROJECT_ROOT__' && ax2 cards read-range --contract '__AX_INPUT_CONTRACT_PATH__' --json The raw source of truth is the only authority. Do not add claims the resolved source ranges or existing cards do not support. Write the candidate card to .ax2-runtime/candidates/ID.md in your working directory, where ID is the contract's contractId with any character outside A-Za-z0-9_- replaced by _. The card must have YAML frontmatter with exactly categoryId, atomicCardId, and title copied from the contract's targetCard, then a # title heading, then these five sections in order: ## WHAT, ## WHERE, ## WHY, ## WHEN, ## HOW. WHAT: 2-4 sentences defining the concept so it stands alone. Specific, complete, no pointers elsewhere. WHERE: map the ecosystem. First list the existing cards with: ls -R library. Write WHERE as a bullet list of relationships. Every genuinely related card that already exists must appear as a wikilink bullet in the form - [[Category - Name]] - relationship phrase, where the link target is the card's file name without .md (for example [[Mechanism - Recurrence Engine]]) and the phrase says why the target matters (provides X, renders Y, governed by Z, feeds W). No naked links: every [[wikilink]] anywhere in the card carries such a phrase. A relationship whose card does not exist yet is written as a plain prose bullet with no brackets, describing the product relationship itself. If the library has no related cards at all, write WHERE entirely as such prose. The card describes the product, never the repository: do not mention the library, the workspace, file listings, or the absence of other cards anywhere in the card. Never invent a card that does not exist to satisfy a link. WHY: why this exists, traced to the product's intent in the source. WHEN: temporal status - when this is active, resets, or applies. HOW: how it behaves or is used, concretely, with at least one example drawn from the source and one anti-example (what this is NOT, per the source's refusals or inadequacies). Answer the contract's atomicity question and nothing else; respect its doNotAnswer list if present. If the run context above shows validator issues or grader feedback from a previous attempt, read your existing candidate first and revise it to address every issue, rather than starting over. Before finishing, check your work with: cd '__AX_PROJECT_ROOT__' && ax2 cards validate-candidate --contract '__AX_INPUT_CONTRACT_PATH__' --json and fix anything it reports. When the candidate file is written and validates, reply with one line: CANDIDATE_READY.
```

### 4. `grade_candidate` — Grade Candidate

Routes besides the golden path: `Bail` → `emit_child_result` · `Revise` → `consume_attempt`

```markdown
You are grading one drafted Alexandria atomic card against its contract and the raw source of truth. You never edit the card. Working directory: the Alexandria workspace. Read only the contract, the candidate, the resolved source ranges, and the card library; do not read any other file in the project. Contract file: '__AX_INPUT_CONTRACT_PATH__'. Read it. The candidate card is at .ax2-runtime/candidates/ID.md where ID is the contractId with any character outside A-Za-z0-9_- replaced by _. Read it. Resolve the exact source ranges with: cd '__AX_PROJECT_ROOT__' && ax2 cards read-range --contract '__AX_INPUT_CONTRACT_PATH__' --json Grade each section 0-100 against this rubric. WHAT: standalone (understandable with no other card), specific (names this product's reality, not generic filler), complete (the concept is fully defined). WHERE: must map the concept's ecosystem as relationships. First run: ls library 2>/dev/null || true to see which cards exist. If the library is empty or missing, links are impossible: never penalize their absence, and score WHERE purely on how well its prose maps the concept's relationships within the product. If related cards do exist, every clearly related one must be linked as [[its file name without .md]] with a relationship phrase, and a missing such link caps WHERE at 70; a wikilink without a phrase is a deficiency; a wikilink to a card that does not exist is a violation. Prose mentions of product concepts are never violations by themselves. sourceGroundingIssues is strictly for claims that materially misstate or invent facts beyond the resolved source ranges. Reasonable restatement or summary of source-supported facts is not a violation; an omission is never a grounding issue; omissions and relationship-mapping problems belong in deficiencies. Statements about the library or workspace inside the card body count as grounding violations. WHY: traces to the product's actual intent as stated in the source, not invented strategy. WHEN: states temporal status truthfully (when active, when it resets, when it applies). HOW: concrete behavior with at least one example grounded in the source and one anti-example; sufficient for a builder to act on. Cross-cutting checks: every factual claim must be supported by the resolved source ranges (list violations in sourceGroundingIssues); the card must answer exactly the contract's atomicity question (one concept, one question); the category must fit (report categoryConfidence). Decide routing. Scores reflect the standard of a strong, source-grounded atomic card, not perfection. The contract's acceptance.minGrade sets the publish bar: A- requires overallScore at least 90 and every section at least 80; B+ requires at least 85 overall and every section at least 75; B requires at least 80 overall and every section at least 70; if the contract states no minGrade, use A-. VERDICT_PUBLISH whenever the bar holds and sourceGroundingIssues is empty; when those hold, do not withhold publish for polish you could still imagine. VERDICT_BAIL only when the card cannot succeed regardless of revision: the source cannot support the contracted card, or the category is fundamentally wrong. Otherwise VERDICT_REVISE, with deficiencies written as specific, actionable revision instructions. Use the routing token names only in the routing field, never in any other field. categoryConfidence is a number from 0 to 100 expressing how well the category fits. When your analysis is done, your final assistant message must be exactly one JSON object matching the required schema and nothing else: no prose, no code fences, no extra fields, and do not end your turn on a tool call. Shape example with placeholder values: {'routing':'VERDICT_REVISE','overallScore':84,'scoreWhat':90,'scoreWhere':80,'scoreWhy':85,'scoreWhen':82,'scoreHow':78,'deficiencies':['...'],'sourceGroundingIssues':[],'categoryConfidence':95} with double quotes instead of single quotes.
```
